c_megalorn.text: A huge, patient creature with antlers the width of a bus. The Irish elk really did have the biggest antlers of any deer, about three and a half metres across.

c_dextera.text: A small, solid, glossy black Dexter cow. It's one of the smallest cattle breeds in Europe, and entirely confident about it.

c_moolet.text: A Dexter calf bounds three steps, stops, and looks round to make sure everyone saw.

boyne_farmer.text: Boyne farmland's some of the richest in Ireland. We've been growing barley here since the Stone Age. The builders of Newgrange ate our porridge, near enough.
A hedgerow's a good thing. A habitat, a windbreak and a road map for hedgehogs.

battle_guide.text: The Battle of the Boyne was in 1690. William of Orange beat James II. It's still in the history books, the songs and every marching season.
I'll say this for the river: it's seen more battles than most, and it's still very peaceful about it.

salmon_fisher.text: The salmon here go out to sea and come back to the same river, years later, and the same stretch of water. They remember the smell of home.
If I'd the Salmon of Knowledge, I'd know where the others are hiding.

tomb_student.text: Newgrange is a mound of earth and stone about 85 metres across, with a corbelled roof that's stayed dry for five thousand years. You'd have to be a very good builder, or very lucky.
I do the maths and I don't believe it. I keep going back to look. It still doesn't add up. Brilliant.

hedge_walker.text: The best way to see the Boyne is on foot. The next best way's by canoe. The worst way's with a map held upside down, which I've tried.
Hedges are Ireland's longest nature reserve. I've no idea who counts them.
